newsitem.title: FRANCE: LVMH says sells 7 pct of Guinness.
newsitem.headline: LVMH says sells 7 pct of Guinness.

text.p: French luxury goods group LVMH said on Friday that it was selling seven percent of Guinness Plc, or a third of its stake in the British drinks group, and would retain 14 percent.
"LVMH is selling seven percent of Guinness," a spokeswoman for LVMH told Reuters.
She said LVMH would retain 14 percent of Guinness and was not seeking any change in their commercial agreements.
The decision to sell part of the Guinness stake reflected a shift in LVMH's business following its 12.9 billion franc purchase of a majority stake in U.S. duty free chain DFS.
LVMH was due to issue a statement shortly.
"The sale of part of the Guinness stake will serve to finance a portion of the DFS acquisition," the spokeswoman said.

Speculation had been rife in the market that LVMH might trim its Guinness stake after making such a large acquisition even though it had the means to finance the DFS deal, as it had equity of 35 billion francs and net debt of three billion.
LVMH confirmed in a statement that it had sold 135,081,327 Guinness shares to Goldman Sachs.
"LVMH intends to retain its remaining 14 percent holding in Guinness and both companies will further develop their business relationships," the statement said.
